issues.t: Automatic transmission loses gears or reverse
issues.sym: The truck slips between gears, flares in RPM, skips from 2nd to 4th, or suddenly has no reverse, 2nd or 4th gear. Fluid may smell burnt.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic (4L60-E) in these trucks is known for worn 3-4 clutches and a sun shell (an internal drum and gear part) that can crack or strip, taking out several gears at once.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell. If gears are missing or it slips, stop towing or hauling and get a transmission shop diagnosis; a rebuild with an upgraded sun shell is the usual fix.

issues.t: Lower ball joints wear out and can separate
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, wandering steering, uneven front tire wear or play in the front wheel. In the worst cases a joint breaks and the wheel folds under.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints on these trucks wear early, especially on 4WD models. A badly worn joint can pull apart.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for ball joint play at every tire rotation once the truck is past 50,000 miles. Replace worn joints right away and get an alignment.

issues.t: Intake manifold gasket leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant goes missing with no puddle, the temperature gauge climbs, the oil looks milky, or there is a sweet smell. The engine may run rough.
issues.why: The original intake manifold gaskets on the 4.3L V6 break down with heat and age and let coolant leak outside or into the engine.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level. If it keeps dropping or the oil looks milky, stop driving and have the gaskets replaced before coolant damages the bearings.

issues.t: Central "spider" fuel injector sticks or leaks
issues.sym: Rough idle right after starting, especially after sitting overnight, long cranking, misfires and a check engine light.
issues.why: These 4.3L engines use one central injector unit with small poppet valves feeding each cylinder. Deposits make the poppets stick, and the unit can leak fuel inside the intake.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes and fuel pressure checked. Replacing the central injector unit (many shops fit the later multi-port style) usually cures it.

issues.t: Rear differential whine or groan
issues.sym: A whine, whir or groan from the back of the truck that gets louder with speed, sometimes with oil seeping from the axle seals.
issues.why: Bearings and gears in the rear axle wear, often after fluid leaks from the pinion or axle seals. Left alone, the noise grows until the differential fails.
issues.next: Check the rear axle fluid level and look for leaks. A shop can tell axle noise from tire or wheel bearing noise; catching it early can save a full rebuild.

issues.t: Rusted brake lines and frame
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid drips near the wheels or under the cab, or heavy rust on the frame and bed mounts.
issues.why: The steel brake lines and frame rust badly on trucks in snow and salt states. A line can rust through and burst under hard braking.
issues.next: Have the brake lines and frame inspected, especially if you live where roads are salted. Replace rusted lines before they fail.

issues.t: Instrument cluster gauges stop working
issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel, temperature or tach gauges stop working, read wrong, or the whole cluster goes dark while driving.
issues.why: The gauge motors and solder joints inside the cluster wear out, and loose connections in the dash wiring can cut power to the cluster.
issues.next: Have the cluster tested. Repair shops can replace the gauge motors or rebuild the cluster for much less than a new one.

issues.t: Key won't turn or ignition switch fails
issues.sym: The key is hard to turn or won't turn at all, gets stuck in the ignition, or the truck won't crank even though the battery is good.
issues.why: The ignition lock cylinder wears with use, and the electrical ignition switch on the column can fail.
issues.next: Don't force the key. A locksmith or shop can replace the lock cylinder or switch; bring all your keys.

issues.t: Heater fan works only on high
issues.sym: The blower fan works on the highest setting only, or not at all on some speeds.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor, which sets the lower fan speeds, burns out. A worn blower motor can overload it.
issues.next: Replace the blower resistor; if the fan motor is noisy or slow, replace it too so the new resistor doesn't fail again.

issues.t: Oil pressure gauge drops or jumps
issues.sym: The oil pressure gauge reads zero, swings around, or the oil light flickers while the engine sounds normal. The sensor may also leak oil.
issues.why: The oil pressure sender on the 4.3L V6 often fails or leaks. Real low oil pressure is less common, but it has to be ruled out.
issues.next: Check the oil level first. Have a shop test the pressure with a mechanical gauge; if it's fine, replacing the sender fixes the reading.

issues.t: Misfire from worn distributor cap and rotor
issues.sym: Misfires, a flashing or steady check engine light, rough idle, hesitation or hard starting.
issues.why: The plastic distributor cap on the 4.3L V6 sits in a hot spot and can warp, crack or rub the rotor. Worn spark plug wires cause similar misfires.
issues.next: Have the cap, rotor and plug wires inspected. Replacing them is a simple first step for misfires on this engine.

issues.t: Engine knock or ping on the 4.3L V6
issues.sym: A light knocking or pinging sound from the engine, often under load or when accelerating.
issues.why: Knock has been widely reported on this generation of the 4.3L V6. Causes include carbon buildup, low-octane fuel and, in some engines, piston wear.
issues.next: Try a tank of better fuel and a carbon cleaning first. If the knock is deep or gets worse, have a shop check for internal wear.

issues.t: Doors sag from worn hinge pins
issues.sym: Doors drop when opened, have to be lifted to latch, or pop and creak when opening and closing.
issues.why: The door hinge pins and bushings wear out over time, especially on the heavy driver's door.
issues.next: Replace the hinge pins and bushings with a repair kit before the worn hinge wears the door striker.

issues.t: Manual transmission could seize and lock the rear wheels (recall)
issues.sym: On affected 5-speed manual trucks the transmission could lock up while driving, locking the rear wheels.
issues.why: A defect in some 5-speed manual transmissions could let them seize. GM recalled the affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN on the NHTSA recall site. A Chevrolet dealer fixes open recalls for free.

issues.t: Brake line can rub on the oil pan (recall)
issues.sym: A brake line touching the oil pan can wear through, causing a fluid leak, a soft pedal and longer stops.
issues.why: On affected trucks a brake line was routed too close to the oil pan and could chafe through.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Have the line rerouted or replaced for free at a dealer.

issues.t: Seat belt webbing may separate (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. In a secondary crash or rollover the belt webbing could tear and fail to hold you.
issues.why: Seat belt webbing on some trucks could be damaged in a crash and separate in a following impact.
issues.next: Check your VIN on the NHTSA recall site and have the belts inspected or replaced by a dealer.

issues.t: Windshield wipers work on and off (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop, run only some of the time, or won't park, often in bad weather.
issues.why: Solder joints on the wiper motor's control board crack, cutting power to the wipers.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open wiper recalls. If it was already done and the wipers act up again, the wiper motor or its control board needs replacing.

issues.t: ABS can lengthen stops in some conditions (recall)
issues.sym: During hard stops with ABS working, the truck may take longer than expected to stop on some surfaces.
issues.why: On affected 4WD trucks a faulty 2WD/4WD switch signal could make the ABS release the brakes more than it should.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer do the free repair.

issues.t: Rear brake hose or pipe can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaks near the rear axle, a soft pedal or a brake warning light.
issues.why: A rear brake line on some 1998 trucks could fatigue and crack, causing a partial loss of braking.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Do not drive with a soft pedal or leaking brakes.

issues.t: Wiring clip near the exhaust can catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: A plastic wiring harness clip near the exhaust manifold could get hot enough to ignite.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the clip replaced for free. Stop and get help if you see smoke.

issues.t: Seat belt buckles may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The buckle base could fail in a crash.
issues.why: Some buckles were not heat-treated properly during manufacture and may be weaker than required.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer replaces the buckles for free.

issues.t: Brake fluid can leak from a faulty seal (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leak, a soft pedal or a brake warning light, with longer stopping distances.
issues.why: A brake system fitting or seal on some trucks was not seated properly and could leak.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer inspect the brake system.

issues.t: ABS spring clip can affect rear brake balance (recall)
issues.sym: An ABS or brake warning light may come on. Normal braking still works, but rear brake balance during hard stops could be affected.
issues.why: A spring clip in the ABS unit on some trucks could cause the system that balances front and rear braking to work incorrectly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer do the repair.

issues.t: Electric S-10 charge port can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A hot or burning smell near the charge port while charging.
issues.why: On the electric S-10, heat could build up at the charging port and start a fire.
issues.next: Stop charging and contact a GM dealer. Check the VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Electric S-10 battery pack can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Battery warning lights come on. If they are ignored, the battery pack can overheat.
issues.why: A problem in the battery pack module on the electric S-10 could lead to overheating and fire if the warning lights were ignored.
issues.next: Never ignore battery warnings on this truck. Check the VIN for open recalls with a GM dealer.

issues.t: Airbag warning label has wrong information (recall)
issues.sym: No driving symptom. A sun visor airbag warning label has incorrect statements.
issues.why: Some trucks were built with an airbag caution label that gives wrong information.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the label for free.
